title: Enterprise RAG and knowledge platforms: Decision Brief
executive_summary: Enterprise RAG and knowledge platforms: coverage 2/3 primary questions, 5 recommendation-safe claims, contradiction count 0.
decision_context: Choose a primary platform for a production pilot in the next two quarters.
key_findings: Azure AI Search is strong when enterprise control, managed infrastructure, and Microsoft ecosystem fit matter. [Evidence: da931a1a-0979-4a5e-8761-7e43b6835722, bff99abc-ec56-4847-bb0c-ae1c3118da3f]

LlamaIndex is strongest as a composable toolkit for teams that want control over ingestion, indexing, routing, and retrieval behavior. [Evidence: 1e4cd1c5-2cd5-451b-bbe9-ec0e10aa2711, 8e4001fd-37ce-46bb-af1c-9ab2d1116cb7]
The cost is higher engineering ownership and a greater need for internal evaluation discipline. [Evidence: 731a972f-5f59-4811-91ed-0bfd6d291ee9, 13d909ca-cab0-48d2-b9b7-0a35c1cce50f]

It offers operational maturity but is infrastructure-first rather than a full research-workflow product by itself. [Evidence: dc6b11a0-0520-4387-a6c3-c87d06621e6a, 3eccd1b6-280e-4044-9460-6953e440ad31]
RAGFlow is positioned around document ingestion and retrieval workflow management rather than only low-level retrieval APIs. [Evidence: 803c2695-e56a-49f0-923d-31f7f3902b3e]
key_risks: Prefer pragmatic operating cost and privacy-aware deployment.
limitations: What are the operational tradeoffs between turnkey and composable stacks?
uncertainty_statement: Evidence quality is sufficient for a directional recommendation, but local validation is still advised.
